description: Chapter_21:145-183 publishes a full `circuit cognitive_memory_board { ... }` build and Chapter_21:7 says real structural queries are run against it. Feed every non-declaration line to the only PCBA parser in the repo.
disposition: CONFIRMED GAP, NOT WAIVED. `cas_forex/pcba_syntax.py` parses exactly one `Component< ... >` expression per call. There is no parser for `circuit`, `cap`, `node`, `charge`, `discharge`, `refresh`, `decode`, `select`, `scan`, or `probe`, and `crc_linter.run_crc` operates on a circuit graph built programmatically in Python, never parsed from CCDL text. The bare `Oscillator< ... >` line parses but compiles to zero CAS leaves. Chapter 21's CCDL listing is therefore pseudocode, not compiler input, and Chapter_21:7's 'we run real structural queries against it' is not true of anything in this codebase. REQUIRED ACTION: either build a CCDL front end or narrow Chapter_21:7. This eval does not close it.

description: The repo's CMB (ccb_designs.py:82-83) stores into `^5^E_{F4}|f`. The published BOM (Chapter_21:28-30, Appendix_D:435-437) publishes cells `^3^P_{F7}|f`, `^6^E_{F4}|A`, `^8^C_{F2}|A`. Check overlap.
disposition: CONFIRMED BOOK CONTRADICTION, OPEN. Appendix_D:413 declares the cell form as `Capacitor< ^5 state, C, leakage >` and Appendix_D:435-437 then publishes three cells, none of them `^5`. The repo sides with the prose; the BOM sides with the state-being-accumulated reading. Chapter 6 has the same split (Chapter_06:44 uses `^5^E_{F4}|f`, Chapter_06:121-123 use `^2^E`, `^3^P`, `^8^C`). A reader cannot tell whether a cell's leaf is the `^5` substrate or the state whose experience it accumulates. This is an owner decision, not a code change, and it is NOT closed by this eval. Both readings compile clean, which is why the compiler cannot catch it.

description: For a device whose read path is 'pick the closest cell', the smallest resolvable distance is the tie-breaking floor. Measure it in both open-simplex implementations.
disposition: MEASURED AND RECORDED, NOT WAIVED. Two opposite artifacts of the same arccos-near-1 sensitivity. The Rust engine cannot certify d=0: for identical vectors the Bhattacharyya coefficient rounds just under 1 and arccos amplifies it. The scaffold Python short-circuits when |1-BC| < 1e-12 (geodesic_memory.py:83), so it returns exactly 0.0 for identical vectors AND for genuinely different ones inside that window. Neither is a bug for belief retrieval; both matter for a 40-cell bank where near-ties decide which memory is recalled. Chapter 21 should state a minimum cell separation. No code change made by this eval.
hoped: both implementations resolve arbitrarily small differences
observed: rust d(v,v)=8.941e-08 (not exactly 0); python d(v, v+1e-12)=0.000e+00 (short-circuits to 0)

description: `cas_forex/cjt_differential.py:55` normalizes its inputs and only rejects NEGATIVE entries, so it silently accepts simplex-boundary vectors containing zeros - exactly the vectors Chapter_21:98 forbids as addresses.
disposition: SCOPE NOTE, NO CODE CHANGE. That function is a CJT divergence heuristic over activation distributions (cjt_analysis.py:55-98), not a CMB address decoder, and normalizing arbitrary non-negative activations is correct for that job. It must NOT be used as the address-decode path: the two implementations that are open-simplex strict (cas_engine, geodesic_memory) are the ones a CMB read path would have to use. Recorded so that a future CMB build does not reach for the nearest available Fisher-Rao function.

description: Chapter_21:117 and :207 specify `nearest(query, bank, metric=fisher_rao)`. No such function exists. The only retrieval function in the repo, `retrieve_by_geodesic_gravity`, ranks by effective_mass / (distance + floor). Put a near-light record and a far-heavy record in front of it and see which comes back first.
disposition: BEHAVIOURAL DIVERGENCE, RECORDED, NOT WAIVED. The gravity ranking is correct for what it was built for - CABS idea-gravity, where a heavy belief is meant to pull from further away - and it is NOT a bug. But it is not the CMB read path the book specifies, and it would return the wrong cell for a CMB query. Consequence for this eval, stated plainly in the report: the pure-distance sort used in the recovery measurements above was WRITTEN BY THIS EVAL, not taken from the repo. The metric is the repo's; the nearest-neighbour selector is not. Chapter_21:117 has no implementation.
observed: rank 1 = far_heavy (near d=0.0991 gravity=10.092; far d=1.7821 gravity=28.057)

description: Chapter_21:275 names 'Lacuna misread as memory' as a failure mode: the system recalls an experience it never had. Check whether the retrieval layer can decline to answer a query with no neighbour.
disposition: CONFIRMED GAP, OPEN. `retrieve_by_geodesic_gravity` has no distance cutoff and no abstain path; it returns top_k results for any legal query. The negative control above shows the DISTANCE is informative (measured above the no-match radius), so an abstain threshold is implementable - it just is not implemented. Chapter 21's own failure mode is therefore live in the only retrieval code that exists. Not closed by this eval, and the eval does not add the threshold to the repo; it only measures that the signal to build one is present.
